cur-kekova-shipwreck.dateNote: An Early Bronze Age wreck about 30 m down off Kekova Island, Antalya, found by a team from Akdeniz University. It is dated to about 4,400-4,700 years ago (roughly 2600-2300 BC) by the style of its amphorae; no wood survives. It carries more than 30 amphorae and 3 stone anchors. The team says it may be the world's oldest known shipwreck: possibly the oldest yet found.
cur-kekova-shipwreck.placeNote: The wreck's exact spot is not published, so it is pinned at Kekova Island's Wikidata point.

cur-legend-achilles.dateNote: Hero of Homer's Iliad. Ancient scholars dated the fall of Troy to about 1184 BCE; the mound at Hisarlik is real and was fought over, but whether the poem describes it is debated.

cur-legend-odysseus.dateNote: Dated, like Achilles, to the traditional date of the Trojan War. Even in antiquity there was argument about which island the poem meant by Ithaca.

cur-legend-aeneas.dateNote: A Trojan of Homer's poem, later made the ancestor of Rome by Virgil writing in the 20s BCE. Dated to the traditional fall of Troy.
